newsitem.title: INDIA: FOCUS-India's ITC snared in forex scandal.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-India's ITC snared in forex scandal.

text.p: India's enforcement directorate on Wednesday arrested a director and three former officials of the country's biggest cigarette company, ITC Ltd, for alleged violation of foreign exchange rules, government authorities said.

The directorate, the watchdog over issues related to corporate finances, made the arrests during early morning searches of offices and homes in four cities -- Calcutta, Bombay, Hyderabad and New Delhi.

"The search operations were organised and undertaken only after sufficient evidence had been collected indicating FERA (Foreign Exchange Regulation Act) violations by ITC Ltd to the tune of over $100 million," a finance ministry statement said.
The ministry statement was received by Reuters in New Delhi.

K.K. Kabirpanthi, deputy director of the enforcement directorate's eastern region, said at a news conference in Calcutta that the foreign exchange violations have been carried out since 1991 and totalled $112 million.
"This is the biggest ever case in the history of the Enforcement Directorate," he said.
Officials of ITC, which controls more than 65 percent of India's tobacco market and among the top 10 Indian companies in terms of turnover, were not immediately available for comment.

Kabirpanthi said enforcement officials would hold R.K. Kutty, chairman and director-in-charge of ITC's international business division, and three former executives in judicial custody until November 13.

The three former executives are Kutty's predecessor, G.K.P. Reddy, R.B. Ravindranath, the former vice-president of ITC's international business division, and M.B. Rao, a former export manager, the finance ministry statement said.
Officials were still questioning Saurav Misra, the company's deputy chairman and J.N. Sapru, a former chairman in Calcutta, Kabirpanthi said.
The New Delhi residence of another former chairman, K.L. Chugh, was also raided and Kabirpanthi said he would be summoned for questioning in Calcutta on Friday.
Current chairman Yogesh Deveshwar was expected to meet enforcement officials when he arrived in Calcutta from New Delhi on Wednesday night or Thursday, officials said.
News of the raids hit ITC's share price. Its price fell sharply, by 18.25 rupees (51.5 U.S. cents) or 5.68 percent, to 303 rupees ($8.54) on the Bombay Stock Exchange.
ITC's overseas share price fell 50 cents to $9.50 on the London Stock Exchange when the government confirmed the arrests.
ITC Ltd is 31.7 percent controlled by Britain's B.A.T Industries Plc. The rest of its shares are held by Indian financial institutions and the public.

The ministry statement said the enforcement authorities also searched the premises of Virginia House, ITC's headquarters in Calcutta and the offices of its global business in the southern city of Hyderabad.
FERA governs all transactions related to foreign exchange in India. It was introduced in the 1970s.
